$comment: Canonical review_conventions AND reviewer_personas parity corpus (ADR-068 / E55.2 / #2243; ADR-084 / E55.8 / #3753 — the persona-* rows, rules in each module's reviewer_personas.go; ADR-084 D2(c) / E55.9 / #3754 — the persona-escalation-* rows, the escalation require.reviewers rungs in the backend's escalation.go and the CLI's validate.go checkEscalations). The review_conventions grammar is validated by TWO implementations that cannot import each other across the backend/cli module wall: the typed backend layer (backend/internal/spec: ParseBytes -> version-routed schema -> typed decode under DisallowUnknownFields -> v2 reuse resolution -> Validate, rules in review_conventions.go) and the CLI's raw-map port (cli/internal/spec: ValidateBytes -> schema -> reuse -> semantic sweep, rules in review_conventions.go). This file is the shared proof surface: each module runs EVERY row through its REAL parse path and asserts the SAME verdict — TestReviewConventionsCorpus_BackendMatches and TestReviewConventionsCorpus_CLIMatches. Row shape: name; optional note; doc (a complete workflow-v2 YAML document); valid; and, for a rejection, layer (schema | semantic) plus path (a JSON pointer). A semantic row also carries message, the EXACT rejection text: the backend's single ValidationError and the CLI's single ValidationErrorEntry must both equal path + message byte for byte. A schema row asserts only that the rejection lands at or under path (the backend reports one leaf, the CLI every leaf). Every rejection row triggers EXACTLY ONE rule, so the backend's first-error and the CLI's full list are comparable; a multi-error document is outside the parity claim. Mirrored verbatim into both modules' testdata/ by scripts/sync-schemas; CI's schema-sync gate red-lines any divergence between the three copies. Named *-fixtures.json (NOT *.schema.json) so the docs/spec/*.schema.json sync loop never globs it.

rows.name: issue-example
rows.note: #2243's own proposal made concrete; applies_to is the shared predicate OBJECT, not the issue sketch's bare glob list (see the applies-to-bare-glob-list row)
rows.doc:
version: "2"
review_conventions:
  backend:
    path: .fishhawk/review/backend.md
  security:
    path: .fishhawk/review/security.md
    applies_to:
      paths: ["backend/internal/crypto/**", "**/policy/**"]
    severity_cap: medium
workflows:
  feature_change:
    stages:
      - id: plan
        type: plan
        executor:
          agent: claude-code
        produces:
          - artifact: plan
            schema: standard_v1
        reviewers:
          agents:
            - provider: anthropic
          conventions: [backend]
      - id: implement
        type: implement
        executor:
          agent: claude-code
        produces:
          - artifact: pull_request
        reviewers:
          agents:
            - provider: anthropic
          conventions: [backend, security]

rows.name: persona-escalation-noop
rows.note: rung 10: every agent-reviewing plan / implement stage already attaches the persona statically, so the escalation raises nothing — refused through the shared MsgFmtEscalationNoRaise shape
rows.doc:
version: "2"
reviewer_personas:

    agent:
      provider: codex
    remit:
      path: docs/review/security-remit.md

  feature_change:

          paths: ["backend/internal/spec/**"]
        require:
          reviewers: [security]
    stages:
      - id: plan
        type: plan
        executor:
          agent: claude-code
        produces:
          - artifact: plan
            schema: standard_v1
        reviewers:
          agents:
            - provider: anthropic
          personas: [security]
      - id: implement
        type: implement
        executor:
          agent: claude-code
        produces:
          - artifact: pull_request
        reviewers:
          agents:
            - provider: anthropic
          personas: [security]
rows.message: workflow "feature_change" escalation 0: require.reviewers: persona "security" does not raise the workflow's baseline: every plan or implement stage that runs agent review already attaches "security" through reviewers.personas, and an escalated persona composes with the static attachment as a de-duplicated union, so the reviewed set is identical to the baseline; an escalation may only ever RAISE a requirement, so one that changes nothing is refused rather than silently accepted as a control that does something. Drop "security" from the static reviewers.personas of some agent-reviewing stage so the escalation attaches it only where a matching change warrants it, or drop "security" from require.reviewers.
